title: The Shipwrecked Woman and Her Child

keywords: the shipwrecked woman and her child
full_text:
A merchant ship sailing from Basra to the Spice Islands encountered a violent cyclone in the middle of the Indian Ocean. The roaring waves broke the rudder, snapped the mainmast, and shattered the vessel upon a jagged coral reef, drowning all the crew save a young mother and her infant child.

Clinging desperately to a floating wooden hatch, the mother was washed ashore upon a tiny, barren sandbank surrounded by the roaring surf. The sandbank possessed neither fresh water, nor green trees, nor shelter from the scorching sun.

The mother wrapped her child in her soaked linen veil, held him close to her breast to shield him from the blazing heat, and lifted her heart in fervent prayer for deliverance.

When the tide rose, threatening to sweep over the low sands, she held the child above her head, standing waist-deep in the churning foam, determined that her infant should breathe even if her own strength failed.

On the third day, when her lips were cracked with salt and her consciousness began to fade, a miraculous sight appeared: a massive, gentle sea turtle, larger than a dining table, swam up to the sandbank and rested upon the shallows.

Seeing the creature, the mother gathered her last ounce of strength, placed her child upon the turtle’s broad shell, and held onto its rim. The ancient creature turned, swam steadily through the breakers, and carried them across three leagues of ocean to the mainland coast, beaching them safely upon a lush, green palm shore where fresh streams flowed into the sea!

A community of kindly fisherfolk rescued them, nursing mother and child back to health. The mother knelt upon the sand, praising the divine providence that protects maternal devotion through the wildest storms of nature.
moral: A mother's selfless love and unwavering faith overcome the fiercest tempests and wildest seas.
